preamble: Assibilation of a fronted (palatalized) voiced velar to the alveolar affricate [dz]. The textbook case is the Slavic second and third (progressive) velar palatalizations, in which *g before or after front vowels was fronted to a palatal and then assibilated to *dz; the affricate survives in the oldest Old Church Slavonic texts, in Lechitic (Polish nodze, pieniądz, ksiądz) and in the Ohrid dialects of Macedonian, elsewhere simplifying to z. Latvian dz from plain *g before front vowels (dzīvs, dzert) is filed under g > dz.

examples.note: *g before the new front vowel *ě was fronted and assibilated; Polish keeps the affricate, while Czech noze has z.
Germanic loanwords in -ing- underwent the third palatalization; Czech peníz has z.
Same development; Czech kněz shows the later simplification dz > z.
